notes: Demo catalog for the Moda preset (demo brand Arvel). 24 pieces in 5 collections of 8/4/4/4/4 (collection grid is 4 columns on desktop, 2 on mobile; 'all' is exactly one page of 24). Names, prices, colors and sold-out sizes follow the Moda mockups. Every on-model shot uses the model reference image so the same woman appears across the catalog.

art_direction.style: Contemporary womenswear e-commerce photography, calm and editorial, realistic fabric texture and drape, natural skin, sharp focus. No text, no logo, no watermark.
art_direction.packshot_rules: Only one person in the frame, no extra people, no props.
art_direction.reference_prompt: Full-length studio portrait of a European woman in her late twenties with fair skin, natural shoulder-length light brown hair with soft waves, light eyes, minimal makeup, relaxed and confident, standing front-facing with arms loose. She wears a plain fitted ecru crewneck and simple straight ecru trousers with flat leather shoes. Seamless warm paper background (#ece7e0), soft diffused daylight from the left, gentle floor shadow.

shots.front: Full-length fashion e-commerce photograph of the woman from the reference image, same face, hair and body, wearing {look} in {color}, styled with {styling}. Standing front-facing in a relaxed natural pose, full body visible from head to toe including the feet, same framing and camera distance as the reference image. Seamless warm paper background (#ece7e0), soft diffused daylight from the left, gentle floor shadow.
shots.back: Show the same woman wearing exactly the same outfit from behind, back view, same pose height and framing. Keep the same garment, color, background, lighting and shadow.
shots.detail: Close-up detail photograph of the {garment} from the reference image, and only the {garment}, not the other clothes, showing its fabric texture, seams and construction. Same color and lighting, warm paper background.
shots.color_swap: Change only the color of the {garment} to {color}. Keep exactly the same woman, pose, framing, background, lighting and every other garment.

pages.title: Our story
pages.body:
Arvel started with a simple frustration: well-made basics that never quite fit. So we built our collection around the cut first, and the label second.

Every piece is pattern-made in our studio and fitted on real bodies in three heights, which is why each product page tells you exactly how it falls and who is wearing it.

We make a small collection each season, in natural and recycled fibers, and we keep the colors calm on purpose: camel, ecru, espresso and black, so everything works together.

pages.title: Stores
pages.body: Visit our showroom by appointment to try pieces on with a stylist. Book a fitting through the contact page and we'll confirm a time within one business day.

articles.title: How to read a size guide
articles.summary: Three measurements that matter more than the label on the tag.
articles.body:
The size on a label is a starting point, not an answer. Three measurements tell you much more: your bust, your natural waist and the widest part of your hips.

Measure over light clothing with a soft tape, keeping it level and snug but not tight. Then compare each number with our size guide.

Finally, read the fit notes on each product. They tell you the model's height, the size she wears and whether the piece runs relaxed or close, which is often the difference between your usual size and the one that actually fits.

articles.title: One coat, five weeks
articles.summary: Wearing the Trinelle from the first cold morning to the last.
articles.body:
We gave the Trinelle wool coat to one of our team for five weeks and asked her to wear it every day.

Week one, it went over a rib knit and wide ecru trousers. By week three it was belted over a slip dress for dinner. On the coldest days it layered over a turtleneck with the collar turned up.

Her verdict: a coat with no buttons sounds impractical until you wear one. The belt does the work, and the dropped shoulders mean there is always room for one more layer.

articles.title: Why our denim runs long
articles.summary: The inseam we chose, and how to hem it at home.
articles.body:
Our Sorrel jeans are cut with an 84 cm inseam, longer than most. That is on purpose: a long leg can always be shortened, but a short one cannot be saved.

To hem them, put them on with the shoes you wear most, fold the hem under to just graze the top of your foot, and pin. Rigid denim holds a clean hem, so a simple single fold is enough.

Prefer to keep the length? Wear them with a small heel, or roll a single cuff for a cropped look.
